newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The absence of any major surprises in Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals' speech coupled with continuing long dollar selling helped the rand gain further ground in busy Tuesday trade.
After trading as high as 4.5325 bid, the rand firmed to 4.5190/5240 against the dollar at the close from 4.5330/5380 on Monday.

Dealers said trade was initially driven by offshore banks selling dollars ahead of Stals' speech -- the contents of which dealers described as "as expected" and "generally neutral" -- as well as dollar demand by importers attracted by the rand's early strength.
In a speech delivered in Pretoria, Stals said that while there was pressure for higher interest rates, he was not convinced that such a move was necessary at this stage.
Some traders voiced concern about Stals' statement that the central bank's net oversold position had grown to over $15 billion.
One trader said the amount would stymie any attempt by the rand to firm beyond the 4.45 level as "the Bank will have to start buying back those dollars at some stage".

Dealers said that after an initial knee-jerk reaction to statements on the bank's forward book, the rand firmed steadily throughout the day, finding a supply of dollars at the 4.53 level and importer demand below the 4.52 level.
One trader added that the rand looked set to target the 4.50 level before the end of the week.
Against the crosses, the rand was last firmer at 7.0358/0481 on sterling from 7.0496/0605 on Monday and at 0.3263/3268 marks from 0.3258/3264 previously.
Trade on the bond market followed a similar pattern to the currency market, with jobbers buying the market up ahead of Stals' speech.
Dealers said there had been initial hopes that Stals would make a concrete announcement on interest rates.
But the yields retraced to an intraday high of 15.56 on what dealers termed Stals' "wishy-washy interest rate views".
Another trader said the reversal of the early run down to the 15.45 percent level had been "a classic case of buy on rumour, sell on fact".

Dealers said there had been a mixture of offshore selling and local institutional buying above the 15.50 level. One trader noted that there had been institutional interest for call options which had spurred further demand in the afternoon.
At the finish, the key R150 was pegged at 15.48 percent from 15.53 percent overnight, while Eskom's 168 was at 15.63 percent from 15,67 percent previously.
The release of second quarter GDP data showing a seasonally adjusted annualised 3.5 percent quarter-on-quarter rise had little effect on the day's trade, after being sidelined by Stals' speech.

Dealers said they would now focus their attention on the release of July trade figures which is due at 0800 GMT on Wednesday and July money supply data which has been tentatively scheduled for release at 1500 GMT on Wednesday.

Bond Exchange figures showed foreigners were net buyers of 41.19 million rand of South African bonds on Monday after buying 27.25 million rand on Friday. Nominal cumulative volumes were pegged at 3.73 billion rand from 7.49 billion rand previously.

On the money market, three-month NCDs were slightly lower at at between 16.60 and 16.75 percent from 16.65 and 16.75 percent on Monday, while 90-day BAs were unmoved at between 16.05 to 16.20 percent.
The Reserve Bank said the money market shortage rose to 8.779 billion rand on Monday from 8.157 billion rand on Saturday.
-- Paul Richardson, Johannesburg newsroom, +27 11 482-1003
